notes: All 30 challenge cards are synthetic and do not increase the real earnings-Q&A count.
No licensed sell-side research, private holdings, transaction records or target-price models were accessed.
Historical materials are methods, not this week’s recommendations.

people.name: Cliff Asness / AQR Capital Management
people.role: AQR co-founder, Managing Principal and CIO; quantitative asset manager and researcher
people.method: Combine valuation spreads with expected fundamental spreads, then reduce tactical confidence when the signal duplicates an existing value exposure
people.boundary: Two coauthored AQR papers support a quantitative method, not current AQR weights, trades or a guarantee that extreme spreads mean-revert on schedule.

people.name: Jeremy Grantham / GMO
people.role: GMO co-founder, board chair and long-term investment strategist
people.method: Separate a technology’s social value from asset valuation, then test price, issuance, investment and career-risk indicators against historical bubble archetypes
people.boundary: Two dated GMO viewpoints support a bubble/technology-cycle framework, not the timing of a trade, the firm’s complete Asset Allocation book or certainty that every innovation bust follows the same path.

people.name: Chuck Akre / Akre Capital Management
people.role: Akre Capital founder and chairman; long-duration public-equity investor
people.method: Reconcile business return on capital, reinvestment runway, dilution and purchase price into growth in real economic value per share
people.boundary: Two dated Akre essays support the compounding framework; they do not disclose a full portfolio, private diligence, current trades or realized future returns.

people.name: Rob Arnott / Research Affiliates
people.role: Research Affiliates founder and board chair; researcher and portfolio manager
people.method: Use starting relative valuation to set long-horizon expected factor returns while retaining timing error and systematic rebalancing discipline
people.boundary: Two coauthored official papers support a factor-allocation method, not live product holdings or a precise market-turn date.

people.name: Dan Rasmussen / Verdad
people.role: Verdad founder, managing partner and portfolio manager
people.method: Replace persuasive narratives with historical base rates, then test AI capital spending through capital-cycle, utilization and required-revenue economics
people.boundary: Two official Verdad essays support a public research method; cited third-party estimates and historical datasets were not fully replicated, and no current position is inferred.

people.name: Sreekrishnan (Krish) Sankarnarayanan / TD Cowen
people.role: TD Cowen semiconductor and semiconductor-equipment analyst at the dated sources
people.method: Demand comparable physical units before translating power, architecture mix or equipment pricing into wafers, revenue and margins
people.boundary: Three public transcript examples across different mechanisms support method samples, not a single repeated personal pattern, licensed TD Cowen forecasts or current rating.

people.name: Mark Murphy / J.P. Morgan
people.role: J.P. Morgan software analyst at the dated source-time evidence
people.method: Test architectural narratives at the workload boundary: silicon mix, site-delivery bottleneck and latency must each map to measurable unit economics
people.boundary: Three attributable exchanges across three calls were manually reviewed for a narrow architecture-to-workload-economics mechanism; this is not a licensed model, permanent persona or current rating.

people.name: Ellie Jiang / Macquarie
people.role: Macquarie internet and platform analyst in source-time and current issuer coverage evidence
people.method: Track scarce AI capital from resource allocation to willingness to pay, financing and cohort return rather than treating all AI workloads as equal
people.boundary: Three attributable questions across three calls were manually reviewed for a narrow resource-allocation-to-return mechanism; no Macquarie report, complete estimates or current recommendation was accessed.

people.name: Ruplu Bhattacharya / BofA Securities
people.role: BofA Securities US IT hardware and technology-supply-chain analyst at the dated evidence
people.method: Bridge physical manufacturing capacity and accepted delivery to revenue, then test whether customer advances and credit facilities make growth genuinely self-funding
people.boundary: Two dated call exchanges support bounded method samples; they do not meet the three-question recurring-pattern threshold and reveal no licensed BofA model or current recommendation.

people.name: Andre Kukhnin / UBS
people.role: UBS industrials/electrical-equipment analyst at both dated Schneider Electric calls
people.method: Turn multi-year data-center and industrial targets into delivery cohorts, capacity gates and revenue acceptance rather than annualizing backlog
people.boundary: Two dated transcript exchanges support method samples only; no recurring personal pattern, complete UBS model, rating rationale or target-price formation is claimed.
